column1: # What each handler of the virtual machine does (docs/pipeline.md).
# handler: method of Obfuscator.VirtualMachine paired with a virtual opcode by CreateHandlerTable;
# cil: the CIL instruction it executes, or vm:<name> for an instruction of the VM only;
# token: the handler in every output of the pipeline (its name is the one of osu!.named.exe);
# uses: occurrences in the 27 virtualized methods (clear part). Read by scripts/devirt.

column9: evidence
GetMethodById(id) then InvokeMethod(method, bool_2: false): non-virtual invocation (CreateInvoker emits OpCodes.Call when the flag is false); callvirt (ExecuteCallvirt) passes true.

LoadLocal(i) pushes a copy (vmethod_3) of vmValue_3[i]; vmValue_3 is the locals array (built by CreateLocalValues from the header locals); index is the byte operand (operand type 9), which separates it from ldloc (ExecuteLdloc, uint16).

CallVirtual: GetMethodById(id), applies a pending constrained. type (constrainedType, set by ExecuteConstrained) then InvokeMethod(method, bool_2: true): virtual invocation with null check; call (ExecuteCall) passes false.

column3: int32 (type 12): bit 31 set = stream position of the callee in the low 30 bits; bit 31 clear = id of a Class92 descriptor (callee position + method id); bit 30 = virtual call
column9: VM-only: call of another virtualized method. Bit 31 set: CallVirtualizedMethod(position, null, null, virt). Otherwise ReadVmToken(id) gives a VmVirtualizedMethodData (descriptor kind 1: int32 position with the same bit 30 flag, int32 method id), CallVirtualizedReference resolves that method only for its generic arguments, then CallVirtualizedMethod. CallVirtualizedMethod reads the callee header at that stream position, pops one value per header parameter ('this' included), runs a new VirtualMachine (ExecuteAtPosition), writes by-ref arguments back and pushes the result unless the callee returns void. Bit 30 (virt): null check on 'this' and, with a pending constrained. type, reflection lookup + InvokeMethod(m, true) instead.

VM-only. PopBlockKey pops an Int64 (top), then an array or object (kind 5 or 7, turned into bytes by SignatureEncoder.GetBytes), then an Int32 (block id); they make a VmBlockKey key. CascadeDecryptor.DecryptStream then reads from the body right after this instruction: 4 encrypted bytes giving the plain length n, then the rest of the block (total (n + 4) rounded up to 4 bytes), decrypts it, and execution continues in the n plain bytes (a CodeBlockFrame pushed on blockStack with its own reader).
